description: Run a script on Amazon Linux 2023 instances to build the LiME kernel module and pre-seed the forensic tool sources

AccessKeyId.description: (Required) AccesskeyID to store evidence details in S3.

SecretAccessKey.description: (Required) SecretAccessKey to store evidence details in S3

SessionToken.description: (Required) SessionToken to store evidence details in S3.

runCommand: #!/bin/bash
# Amazon Linux 2023 forensic tool pre-seeder: builds the LiME module for the
# builder's own kernel and uploads it with the LiME and volatility3 sources, so
# a memory acquisition on a matching kernel does not have to compile anything on
# the instance under investigation.
# Like the AL2023 symbol document this fails loudly. The Amazon Linux 2 version
# exited 0 whether or not the module was ever produced, so a deployment reached
# CREATE_COMPLETE with nothing usable in the evidence bucket.
# Upstream versions, pinned. An unpinned clone builds whatever is at the tip of
# the default branch on the day of the incident - into the tooling that produces
# and reads forensic evidence. These match the pins already used by the
# acquisition and investigation documents so that one release means one set of
# tool versions. Note 504ensicsLabs/LiME redirects to jtsylve/LiME, its original
# author; cloning the old path works only while GitHub honours that redirect.
LIME_REF=v1.12.0
VOL3_REF=v2.28.0
set -o pipefail
fail() { echo "TOOL_BUILD_FAILED: $1" >&2; exit 1; }
kernel_release=$(uname -r)
# AL2023 names kernel sub-packages per kernel line (kernel6.18-devel) from 6.12
# onwards, but keeps the unversioned name (kernel-devel) on the 6.1 line.
kernel_line=$(uname -r | cut -d. -f1,2)
echo "building forensic tools for ${kernel_release} (line ${kernel_line})"
grep -q 'platform:al2023' /etc/os-release || fail "not an Amazon Linux 2023 instance: $(. /etc/os-release; echo $PRETTY_NAME)"
# /tmp is a RAM-backed tmpfs on AL2023 capped at ~50% of memory; the two source
# trees, the kernel build tree and the module do not reliably fit there.
workdir=/var/tmp/forensic-tools-builder
sudo rm -rf $workdir && mkdir -p $workdir && cd $workdir || fail 'cannot create work directory'
# git, gcc, make and zip are all absent from the AL2023 AMI, and the LiME
# Makefile needs a compiler plus the headers for the running kernel. awscli is
# deliberately not installed: AL2023 ships awscli-2 and there is no awscli
# package in its repositories.
sudo dnf install -y -q git gcc make zip || fail 'unable to install build tools'
install_kernel_devel() {
# Pin the running kernel release: a kernel-devel for any other release
# would build a module the acquisition cannot insert.
sudo dnf install -y -q "kernel${kernel_line}-devel-${kernel_release}" >/dev/null 2>&1 && { echo "installed kernel${kernel_line}-devel-${kernel_release}"; return 0; }
sudo dnf install -y -q "kernel-devel-${kernel_release}" >/dev/null 2>&1 && { echo "installed kernel-devel-${kernel_release}"; return 0; }
return 1
install_kernel_devel || fail "no kernel-devel package for ${kernel_release}"
test -d /lib/modules/${kernel_release}/build || fail "no kernel build tree for ${kernel_release} - cannot compile LiME"
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID={{AccessKeyId}}
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY={{SecretAccessKey}}
export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN={{SessionToken}}
export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION={{Region}}
aws configure set default.s3.max_concurrent_requests 20
cd $workdir || fail 'cannot enter work directory'
git clone --depth 1 --branch "$LIME_REF" https://github.com/jtsylve/LiME.git || fail "LiME clone of $LIME_REF failed"
# The acquisition document unzips this into a LiME directory, so archive the
# directory itself rather than its contents.
zip -q -r LiME.zip LiME || fail 'LiME source archive failed'
test -s $workdir/LiME.zip || fail 'LiME source archive is empty'
aws s3 cp $workdir/LiME.zip s3://{{s3bucket}}/tools/LiME/ --acl bucket-owner-full-control || fail 's3 upload of the LiME source failed'
echo "s3 copy complete: s3://{{s3bucket}}/tools/LiME/LiME.zip"
cd $workdir/LiME/src || fail 'LiME source tree missing'
make || fail 'LiME module build failed'
# Name the module lime-<uname -r>.ko: that is the object the memory
# acquisition document looks for before falling back to compiling on the
# instance under investigation.
module=lime-${kernel_release}.ko
# Only upload a module that actually built. Copying unconditionally used to
# publish nothing on failure while the step still reported success.
test -s $module || fail "LiME build produced no ${module}"
echo "LiME module built: $(ls -lh $module | awk '{print $5}')"
aws s3 cp $module s3://{{s3bucket}}/tools/LiME/$module --acl bucket-owner-full-control || fail 's3 upload of the LiME module failed'
echo "s3 copy complete: s3://{{s3bucket}}/tools/LiME/$module"
cd $workdir || fail 'cannot return to work directory'
git clone --depth 1 --branch "$VOL3_REF" https://github.com/volatilityfoundation/volatility3.git || fail "volatility3 clone of $VOL3_REF failed"
zip -q -r volatility3.zip volatility3 || fail 'volatility3 source archive failed'
test -s $workdir/volatility3.zip || fail 'volatility3 source archive is empty'
aws s3 cp $workdir/volatility3.zip s3://{{s3bucket}}/tools/volatility3/ --acl bucket-owner-full-control || fail 's3 upload of the volatility3 source failed'
echo "s3 copy complete: s3://{{s3bucket}}/tools/volatility3/volatility3.zip"
sudo rm -rf $workdir
exit 0;
